title: Hash chain and internal TIP names (batch p1-G07-2: circl_hashlookup, yaraify, file_hashing, misp/opencti/thehive_sightings)

attributes.file_name: file name(s) of the sample as reported by the source (known-file record or submissions); untrusted text
attributes.md5: MD5 digest of the file (computed locally, or reported by the source for the same file)
attributes.sha1: SHA-1 digest of the file (computed locally, or reported by the source for the same file)
attributes.sha256: SHA-256 digest of the file (computed locally, or reported by the source for the same file)
attributes.sha512: SHA-512 digest of the file (computed locally, or reported by the source for the same file)
attributes.sha3_384: SHA3-384 digest of the sample as reported by the source
attributes.crc32: CRC32 checksum of the file as reported by a known-file set
attributes.known_file: label 'known file: <product/OS> (<set>)' from a known-file database: presence in a software set, never a 'clean' verdict
attributes.known_file_set: known-file set of the record: nsrl | os_package | snap | other
attributes.known_malicious: sources a known-file database lists the hash as malicious in (e.g. malshare.com)
attributes.product: software product the file ships with per a known-file record {name, version, vendor_code, ...}
attributes.operating_system: operating system named by a known-file record {name, version, code}
attributes.package: OS package that ships the file {name, version, release, arch}
attributes.hashlookup_trust: CIRCL hashlookup trust score 0-100 (presence across known-file sets, not goodness)
attributes.dual_use: offensive-security or dual-use software named by the record (e.g. BlackArch, Metasploit): never known-good
attributes.yara_rules: YARA rule names a source reports as matching the file
attributes.family_hints: malware family names suggested by rule names but not confirmed by the alias index (low confidence)
attributes.submission_count: number of times the sample was submitted to the source (e.g. YARAify 'sightings')
attributes.hash_identification: hash-type identification of the value {primary, readings, alternatives, ambiguous, note}: identification only, never cracking or plaintext lookup
attributes.internal_sightings: hits in the organisation's own TIP/case platforms [{platform, ref, org, tlp, date, verdict}] (MISP, OpenCTI, TheHive)
attributes.tip_score: score the internal TIP gives the value (OpenCTI x_opencti_score 0-100, MISP decay score)
attributes.similarity_hashes: similarity/structural hashes of a file: {imphash, tlsh, ssdeep, telfhash, gimphash, dhash_icon}
attributes.av_signatures: antivirus signature names a source reports for the file (e.g. ClamAV)
attributes.allowlisted: list of allow-list reasons a source gives for the entity (whitelist, known false positive, warninglist)
attributes.threat_actors: threat actor / adversary names a source associates with the entity (community labels unless stated otherwise)
attributes.attack_techniques: MITRE ATT&CK technique ids a source associates with the entity

tags.internal_sighting: seen in the organisation's own TIP or case platform (MISP, OpenCTI, TheHive): 'known internally'
tags.false_positive: the source marks the value as a false positive (e.g. a MISP false-positive sighting)
tags.historical: listing or observation older than 30 days, removed or from a frozen list: not current state
tags.warninglist: the value is on a warninglist of the source (likely benign or noisy)
tags.test_file: antivirus test file (EICAR): detections are expected and not an incident
tags.conflict: sources disagree (e.g. a known file that a specific source lists as malicious or vulnerable)

relations.same_file: file hash -> another hash (md5/sha1/sha256) of the same file
relations.contained_in: file hash -> hash of the package, archive or snap that contains the file
relations.contains: package or archive hash -> hash of a file inside it
relations.unpacked_to: packed sample -> payload unpacked from it by the source's unpacker
relations.has_hash: local file -> digest computed from its content
relations.alternate_reading: ambiguous input -> the same characters read as another entity type (e.g. SHA-256 vs certificate fingerprint)

notes: similarity_hashes, yara_rules, av_signatures, allowlisted, threat_actors and attack_techniques, the tag historical and the relation same_file are re-declared with the exact descriptions of the batches that declared them first (p1-G07-1, p1-G03-1): same meaning, first declaration wins.
